fields.title: The Hobbit
fields.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
fields.description: Bilbo Baggins, a comfort-loving hobbit, is swept into an epic quest by the wizard Gandalf and a company of thirteen dwarves to reclaim their mountain home from the dragon Smaug. Along the way he discovers courage, resourcefulness, and a mysterious magic ring that will change the world forever. Tolkien's richly imagined Middle-earth comes alive through vivid landscapes and unforgettable characters. This beloved classic laid the foundation for modern fantasy literature.

fields.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
fields.author: Harper Lee
fields.description: Narrated by the young Scout Finch, the novel follows her father Atticus, a principled lawyer in a small Alabama town who agrees to defend a Black man falsely accused of raping a white woman during the racially charged 1930s. Through Scout's innocent eyes, the story explores the deep injustice, hypocrisy, and moral complexity of the American South with both tenderness and unflinching honesty. The mysterious recluse Boo Radley and the quiet heroism of Atticus have become two of the most enduring figures in all of American fiction. It won the Pulitzer Prize in 1961 and has sold more than 45 million copies worldwide.

fields.title: The Name of the Wind
fields.author: Patrick Rothfuss
fields.description: Kvothe, a legendary figure of myth and magic, narrates the story of his own extraordinary life to a traveling scribe. From his humble beginnings as the son of traveling performers, he rises to become the most notorious wizard of his age. His journey takes him through poverty, loss, and the pursuit of forbidden knowledge at a prestigious university. This is the first volume of the Kingkiller Chronicle, a masterwork of modern fantasy.

fields.title: Dune
fields.author: Frank Herbert
fields.description: Set in a distant future, Dune follows young Paul Atreides as his noble family takes control of the desert planet Arrakis, the only source of the most valuable substance in the universe. Betrayal, political intrigue, and survival in a harsh environment shape Paul into something far greater than a mere heir. The story weaves ecology, religion, and power into one of the greatest science fiction epics ever written. It remains the best-selling science fiction novel of all time.

fields.title: Sapiens
fields.author: Yuval Noah Harari
fields.description: Harari traces the entire history of humankind from the emergence of Homo sapiens in Africa to the present day. He argues that what sets humans apart is our ability to believe in shared myths — money, nations, religions — that allow mass cooperation on an unprecedented scale. The book challenges readers to question the assumptions behind modern society, progress, and happiness. It is a sweeping, provocative, and brilliantly readable account of how we came to rule the world.

fields.title: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone
fields.author: J.K. Rowling
fields.description: Harry Potter, an orphan living miserably with his aunt and uncle, discovers on his eleventh birthday that he is a wizard and has been accepted to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. In the magical world he never knew existed, he finds friendship, belonging, and the truth about his parents' mysterious deaths at the hands of the dark lord Voldemort. Together with his friends Ron and Hermione, Harry uncovers a plot to steal a powerful artifact hidden deep within the school. It is the first chapter of one of the most beloved and widely read fantasy series in the history of literature.

fields.title: The Alchemist
fields.author: Paulo Coelho
fields.description: Santiago, a young Andalusian shepherd, embarks on a journey to find a treasure he has dreamed of, traveling across Spain and the Egyptian desert. Along the way he encounters merchants, Englishmen, and an alchemist who teach him the language of the world and the importance of listening to his heart. Coelho's slim, fable-like novel is a meditation on destiny, courage, and the cost of following one's dreams. It has sold over 65 million copies and been translated into 80 languages.

fields.author: George Orwell
fields.description: Winston Smith lives under the crushing surveillance of Big Brother in a totalitarian society where thought itself is a crime. He secretly rebels by falling in love and seeking the truth buried beneath layers of propaganda and rewritten history. Orwell's vision of a world stripped of privacy, truth, and individual freedom remains one of the most chilling and prophetic novels ever written. Its concepts of doublethink, Newspeak, and the Thought Police have become permanently embedded in modern culture.

fields.title: The Great Gatsby
fields.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
fields.description: Narrated by the observant Nick Carraway, the novel follows the mysterious millionaire Jay Gatsby and his obsessive pursuit of the beautiful Daisy Buchanan in the glittering excess of 1920s New York. Fitzgerald captures the hollow glamour of the Jazz Age and the dark underside of the American Dream with lyrical, unforgettable prose. Gatsby's parties, his green light, and his tragic end have become some of the most iconic images in American literature. It is a timeless story of ambition, illusion, and the impossibility of recapturing the past.

fields.title: Pride and Prejudice
fields.author: Jane Austen
fields.description: Elizabeth Bennet, the sharp-witted second daughter of a country gentleman, navigates the pressures of marriage, class, and society in Regency-era England. Her sparring relationship with the proud and wealthy Mr. Darcy evolves from mutual disdain into one of literature's most celebrated romances as both characters confront their own prejudices and pride. Austen's razor-sharp observations on social conventions, family dynamics, and the limited choices available to women remain as relevant and entertaining today as ever. It is widely considered the finest novel in the English language and has never been out of print since its first publication.

fields.title: The Fellowship of the Ring
fields.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
fields.description: Frodo Baggins inherits a plain gold ring that turns out to be the One Ring of the Dark Lord Sauron. With eight companions he sets out from the Shire to destroy it in the fires where it was forged. The first part of The Lord of the Rings, it moves from cosy hobbit holes to the mines of Moria and the breaking of the fellowship.

fields.title: A Game of Thrones
fields.author: George R.R. Martin
fields.description: When Lord Eddard Stark is summoned south to serve the king, his family is drawn into a deadly struggle for the Iron Throne. Far to the north, an ancient threat stirs beyond the Wall, and across the sea an exiled princess plans her return. Told through many points of view, it is a sprawling tale of power, loyalty and betrayal.

fields.title: The Catcher in the Rye
fields.author: J.D. Salinger
fields.description: Expelled from his prep school, sixteen-year-old Holden Caulfield spends a few aimless days in New York City before going home. His sharp, funny and wounded voice rails against the phoniness of the adult world while he struggles with grief and loneliness. It remains one of the defining novels of adolescence.

fields.title: Brave New World
fields.author: Aldous Huxley
fields.description: In the World State, people are engineered in hatcheries, conditioned from birth and kept content with pleasure and the drug soma. When Bernard Marx brings a young man raised outside the system back to London, its comforts start to look like a cage. Huxley's vision of a society controlled by happiness rather than fear still feels startlingly current.

fields.title: Fahrenheit 451
fields.author: Ray Bradbury
fields.description: Guy Montag is a fireman, and in his world firemen burn books. A chance meeting with a curious young neighbour makes him question everything he has been taught. Bradbury's short, urgent novel is a warning about censorship and a culture that would rather be entertained than think.

fields.title: The Handmaid's Tale
fields.author: Margaret Atwood
fields.description: In the Republic of Gilead, a theocracy that has replaced the United States, Offred is a Handmaid whose only purpose is to bear children for a powerful Commander. She remembers a time when she had a job, a family and her own name. Quiet, precise and chilling, the novel shows how quickly freedoms can be taken away.

fields.title: Foundation
fields.author: Isaac Asimov
fields.description: Mathematician Hari Seldon predicts that the Galactic Empire will fall and thirty thousand years of chaos will follow. To shorten the dark age he founds a colony of scholars at the edge of the galaxy. The stories that follow trace how reason, trade and cunning keep his plan alive across generations.

fields.title: Neuromancer
fields.author: William Gibson
fields.description: Case was the best hacker in the business until he crossed the wrong people and lost the ability to jack into cyberspace. A mysterious employer offers to repair him in exchange for one more job. Gibson's debut coined much of the language of cyberpunk and imagined the networked world before it existed.

fields.title: The Martian
fields.author: Andy Weir
fields.description: After a dust storm forces his crew to evacuate, astronaut Mark Watney is left for dead on Mars. With limited supplies and no way to call home, he has to science his way to survival, one problem at a time. Funny and fiercely practical, it is a celebration of ingenuity under pressure.

fields.title: Project Hail Mary
fields.author: Andy Weir
fields.description: Ryland Grace wakes up alone on a spaceship with no memory of how he got there or why. Slowly he remembers that he is humanity's last chance to stop a microbe that is dimming the Sun. An unexpected friendship far from home turns a survival story into something warmer.

fields.title: Educated
fields.author: Tara Westover
fields.description: Tara Westover grew up in the mountains of Idaho, in a survivalist family that kept her out of school and away from doctors. She taught herself enough to get into university, and went on to earn a PhD from Cambridge. Her memoir is about the cost of leaving home, and what it takes to see the world for yourself.

fields.title: Atomic Habits
fields.author: James Clear
fields.description: Small habits, repeated every day, add up to remarkable results. James Clear explains how habits form and gives practical ways to make good ones easier and bad ones harder. The book focuses on systems rather than goals, and on becoming the kind of person who does the thing.

fields.title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
fields.author: Daniel Kahneman
fields.description: Nobel laureate Daniel Kahneman describes two ways of thinking: a fast, intuitive system and a slow, deliberate one. He shows how the fast system leads us into predictable errors when we judge risk, plan, or make choices. Drawing on decades of research, it changes how you see your own decisions.

fields.title: The Road
fields.author: Cormac McCarthy
fields.description: A father and his young son walk south through a burned and empty America, pushing a shopping cart of supplies and avoiding the people who remain. They have nothing but each other and the idea that they are carrying the fire. Spare and devastating, it won the Pulitzer Prize.

fields.title: The Kite Runner
fields.author: Khaled Hosseini
fields.description: Amir, the son of a wealthy man in Kabul, grows up alongside Hassan, his father's servant's son and his closest friend. One act of cowardice in the winter of 1975 haunts him for decades, through war, exile and a new life in America. A story of friendship, guilt and the chance to be good again.

fields.title: Jane Eyre
fields.author: Charlotte Brontë
fields.description: Orphaned and mistreated as a child, Jane Eyre becomes a governess at Thornfield Hall, where she falls in love with its brooding master, Mr Rochester. A secret in the house threatens everything. Brontë's heroine, plain, poor and fiercely independent, insists on being treated as an equal.

fields.title: Moby-Dick
fields.author: Herman Melville
fields.description: Ishmael signs on to the whaling ship Pequod, only to discover that Captain Ahab has one goal: revenge on the white whale that took his leg. The voyage becomes an obsession that will consume the ship and its crew. Part adventure, part encyclopaedia of the sea, it is one of the great American novels.

fields.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
fields.author: Stieg Larsson
fields.description: Disgraced journalist Mikael Blomkvist is hired by an ageing industrialist to find out what happened to his niece, who vanished forty years ago. He teams up with Lisbeth Salander, a brilliant and guarded hacker. Their investigation uncovers a family's dark secrets and a long trail of violence.

fields.title: Gone Girl
fields.author: Gillian Flynn
fields.description: On the morning of their fifth wedding anniversary, Amy Dunne disappears, and her husband Nick quickly becomes the prime suspect. Told in turns by Nick and by Amy's diary, the story keeps changing shape. A sharp, twisting thriller about marriage and the stories people tell about themselves.

fields.title: And Then There Were None
fields.author: Agatha Christie
fields.description: Ten strangers are invited to an island off the Devon coast, each with a past they would rather forget. Cut off from the mainland, they begin to die one by one, following the lines of an old nursery rhyme. Christie's best-selling mystery is a masterclass in tension.

fields.title: The Night Circus
fields.author: Erin Morgenstern
fields.description: The circus arrives without warning and is open only at night, its black-and-white tents full of impossible wonders. Behind the scenes, two young magicians, Celia and Marco, are bound to a contest they don't fully understand. Lush and dreamlike, it is a love story set in a place built of illusions.

fields.title: Circe
fields.author: Madeline Miller
fields.description: Born to the sun god Helios, Circe is mocked by her family until she discovers the power of witchcraft. Banished to an island, she meets gods, monsters and mortals, among them Odysseus. Miller retells Greek myth from the point of view of a woman who learns to choose her own fate.

fields.title: The Hunger Games
fields.author: Suzanne Collins
fields.description: In Panem, the Capitol forces each district to send two teenagers to fight to the death on live television. When her younger sister is chosen, Katniss Everdeen volunteers to take her place. Fast-paced and gripping, it is a story about survival, spectacle and defiance.

fields.title: Where the Crawdads Sing
fields.author: Delia Owens
fields.description: Abandoned by her family, Kya Clark grows up alone in the marshes of North Carolina, learning from the gulls and the tides. Years later, when a local man is found dead, the townspeople suspect the Marsh Girl. Part coming-of-age story and part courtroom drama, it is steeped in the natural world.
